title: San Francisco
description: Fog, hills, and Painted Ladies — how well do you know the City by the Bay?

questions.prompt: Which San Francisco neighborhood was the epicenter of the 1967 'Summer of Love' counterculture movement?
questions.explanation: Haight-Ashbury — the intersection of Haight and Ashbury streets — drew tens of thousands of young people during the 1967 Summer of Love (Wikipedia: 'Summer of Love').

questions.prompt: Which neighborhood is historically known as San Francisco's 'Little Italy'?
questions.explanation: North Beach has been the city's Italian-American enclave since the late 1800s, and still hosts the annual North Beach Festival (Wikipedia: 'North Beach, San Francisco').

questions.prompt: Which San Francisco Bay island housed a federal penitentiary from 1934 to 1963?
questions.explanation: Alcatraz operated as a federal maximum-security prison from 1934 to 1963 and is now managed by the National Park Service (nps.gov/alca; Wikipedia: 'Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary').

questions.prompt: Coit Tower atop Telegraph Hill was funded by a 1929 bequest from which San Francisco socialite?
questions.explanation: Lillie Hitchcock Coit left a third of her estate to the city 'for the purpose of adding to the beauty of San Francisco'; the tower opened in 1933 (Wikipedia: 'Coit Tower').

questions.prompt: Which San Francisco bakery, founded in 1849, claims to be the city's original sourdough?
questions.explanation: Boudin Bakery has baked sourdough in San Francisco since 1849 using a mother dough that traces back to its founding (boudinbakery.com/our-story; Wikipedia: 'Boudin Bakery').

questions.prompt: Which seafood stew, created by Italian immigrant fishermen at Fisherman's Wharf in the late 1800s, is considered a San Francisco original?
questions.explanation: Cioppino was developed by Ligurian fishermen working out of Fisherman's Wharf, combining the day's catch with tomato and wine (Wikipedia: 'Cioppino').
